name: Anti-NXP2 Dermatomyositis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology (EULAR/ACR) Classification Criteria for Dermatomyositis

criteria.description: Presence of anti-NXP2 autoantibodies detected by immunoprecipitation or ELISA
Symmetric proximal muscle weakness affecting limb girdle muscles
Typical dermatomyositis skin manifestations including heliotrope rash or Gottron papules
Presence of subcutaneous or intramuscular calcinosis detected clinically or radiologically
Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) or aldolase levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anti-NXP2 antibodies plus symmetric proximal muscle weakness with or without characteristic skin rash
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Calcinosis is more frequent in juvenile cases and may aid diagnosis

searchTerms: equal muscle weakness on both sides
heart muscle inflammation and irregular heartbeat
heart rhythm problems with heart inflammation
heart involvement causing arrhythmias and myocarditis

laboratory: Anti-NXP2 autoantibodies detected by immunoprecipitation or ELISA
Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) and aldolase
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: MRI showing muscle edema and inflammation
High-resolution CT for interstitial lung disease assessment
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; autoantibody association is key
other: Muscle biopsy showing perifascicular atrophy and inflammatory infiltrates

distinguishingFeatures: Higher risk of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease
Different patterns of skin involvement and calcinosis
Absence of characteristic dermatomyositis skin rash

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness leading to respiratory failure
Development of extensive calcinosis causing ulcerations or infections
Signs of cardiac involvement such as arrhythmias or myocarditis
references: Betteridge Z, McHugh N. Myositis-specific autoantibodies: an important tool to support diagnosis of myositis. J Intern Med. 2016.
Sato S, Kuwana M. Clinical features and pathogenesis of anti-NXP2 antibody-positive dermatomyositis. Curr Rheumatol Rep. 2019.
EULAR/ACR Classification Criteria for Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies. Ann Rheum Dis. 2017.
